title: Santa Clarita Valley seats in the Assembly, State Senate and U.S. House, by redistricting plan
status: research only; nothing written to the database

valley_definition.used: The Census Bureau county subdivision Newhall CCD (census tracts 9200 to 9203: the City of Santa Clarita, Castaic, Stevenson Ranch, Val Verde, Hasley Canyon, Green Valley and the unincorporated land around them) plus the Agua Dulce CDP. For the 1991 plan, measured on 2000 blocks, the City of Santa Clarita as it stood in 2000 is added, because about 10,200 city residents then sat in tract 9108 outside the Newhall CCD; the rest of tract 9108 (Agua Dulce area, not yet a CDP in 2000) is counted with the valley.
valley_definition.acton: Acton is reported separately and not used to decide main or partial. It sits in the South Antelope Valley CCD, across the Sierra Pelona divide. It never changes the answer: in every plan it falls in a district already listed, except the 2001 plan where part of Acton was in AD 36 (Acton only, no valley population).
valley_definition.green_valley: Green Valley CDP (about 1,000 people) is inside the Newhall CCD but sits at the head of Bouquet and San Francisquito canyons; districts that hold only Green Valley are marked fringe.
valley_definition.method: Every census block in the valley was assigned to its district from official block equivalency files (Statewide Database for 1991, 2001 and 2011 plans) or by point-in-polygon against Census TIGERweb district boundaries (2021 plan and the 2025 congressional map, and as a cross-check for 2001 and 2011, which matched exactly). Population weights: 2000 Census for the 1991 plan, 2010 Census for 2001 and 2011, 2020 Census for 2021 and 2025.

term_rule: Term dates: state legislative terms begin the first Monday in December after the election (Cal. Const. art. IV sec. 2(a)(3)); U.S. House terms begin January 3.

main_seat_numbers.note: 38 carried over from the 2001 plan into the 2011 plan, so 2012 changed the lines but not the number

assembly.split_now: Yes, lightly. AD 40 holds 98 percent of the valley (the whole City, Castaic, Stevenson Ranch, Val Verde, Hasley Canyon). AD 34 holds Agua Dulce and about 1,700 people in unincorporated land north of the City (upper Bouquet Canyon and Green Valley area, and the hills north of Castaic), plus Acton.

senate.stagger_note: Senate terms are four years and staggered (odd-numbered districts elected in presidential years). A new plan reaches odd-numbered districts only at the next presidential-year election, so the 2011 plan reached the valley in 2012 and the 2021 plan only in 2024. From December 2022 to December 2024 the valley was still represented by Scott Wilk (21st) and Henry Stern (27th), elected in 2020 on the 2011 lines.

people_checked.name: Cameron Smyth
people_checked.finding: Confirmed. Elected 2006, 2008, 2010; served 4 Dec 2006 to 3 Dec 2012 (Record: 2007-2012). 2001-plan AD 38, the main valley seat.

people_checked.name: Scott Wilk
people_checked.finding: Confirmed. AD 38 (2011 plan) 3 Dec 2012 to 5 Dec 2016; SD 21 5 Dec 2016 to 2 Dec 2024 (elected 2016, 2020).

people_checked.name: Dante Acosta
people_checked.finding: Confirmed. Elected 2016; lost to Christy Smith 2018.

people_checked.name: Christy Smith
people_checked.finding: Confirmed: 3 Dec 2018 to 7 Dec 2020. Lost CD 25 special (12 May 2020), CD 25 general (Nov 2020, by 333 votes) and CD 27 (Nov 2022) to Mike Garcia.

people_checked.name: Suzette Martinez Valladares
people_checked.finding: Assembly 38th, 7 Dec 2020 to 5 Dec 2022: confirmed. Assembly 40th: NOT held; she lost the first 40th-District election (Nov 2022) to Pilar Schiavo, 79,852 to 79,330. Senate 23rd from 2 Dec 2024: confirmed (won Nov 2024, 52.4%).

people_checked.name: Pilar Schiavo
people_checked.finding: Holds AD 40, the valley main seat, since 5 Dec 2022; re-elected 2024; first in June 2026 primary. Nathan's note that Valladares holds the 40th is not right.

people_checked.name: Patsy Ayala
people_checked.claim: City: "served in the California State Assembly and Senate"
people_checked.finding: Staff, not a member. She is absent from both official Records of Members (only Ruben S. Ayala, a San Bernardino senator 1974-1998, appears). A June 2014 KHTS/SCVNews report has Assemblyman Wilk naming her field representative in his district office; her College of the Canyons bio says she worked for Senator Wilk and Assemblywoman Valladares.

people_checked.name: Buck McKeon
people_checked.claim: U.S. House 1993 to 2015, district 25 then 25 again?
people_checked.finding: Confirmed: 3 Jan 1993 to 3 Jan 2015, and the number was 25 under all three plans (1991, 2001, 2011). Did not run in 2014.

people_checked.name: Tom Lackey
people_checked.finding: Partial-district member only: AD 36 (2011 plan) 1 Dec 2014 to 5 Dec 2022; AD 34 (2021 plan) 5 Dec 2022 to 7 Dec 2026. Termed out 2026.

people_checked.name: Steve Knight
people_checked.finding: All three confirmed. AD 36 2008-2012 was the 2001-plan 36th, which held only part of Acton, not the valley proper. SD 21 3 Dec 2012 to resignation 5 Jan 2015 (main seat). CD 25 3 Jan 2015 to 3 Jan 2019 (main seat); lost to Katie Hill 2018; ran again in the 2020 special primary (17.1%, third).

people_checked.name: Sharon Runner
people_checked.finding: AD 36 2002-2008 (2001-plan 36th: Acton only). SD 17 by special primary 15 Feb 2011 to Dec 2012 (main seat). SD 21 by special primary 17 Mar 2015 to death in office 14 Jul 2016 (main seat).

people_checked.name: George Runner
people_checked.finding: AD 36 2 Dec 1996 to 2 Dec 2002: this was the 1991-plan 36th, then the MAIN valley Assembly seat (the whole City). SD 17 6 Dec 2004 to resignation 21 Dec 2010 (main seat), to the Board of Equalization.

people_checked.name: Pete Knight
people_checked.finding: AD 36 7 Dec 1992 to 2 Dec 1996 (main seat, 1991 plan). SD 17 2 Dec 1996 to death in office 7 May 2004 (main seat).
